title: Canary tokenizer + config drift rollback notes
body:
Executive summary (short):

On 2025-11-06 21:14:00 UTC we observed a canary rollout for model blueprint-v2.1 producing malformed token sequences for ~18% of requests routed to the canary pool. A downstream consumer (chat-service) rejected these responses and returned 500s for a subset of traffic. Impact was confined to the canary pool and accounted for ~0.4% of total production traffic but caused elevated error rates on the chat-service and alerted on SLA thresholds. Root causes: tokenizer version mismatch between the model artifact and the canary-serving config, plus a subtle config drift where the fallback tokenizer path in the environment pointed to an older token vocab (vocab_v1) instead of vocab_v2.1. A secondary contributing factor was a packaging error in the model bundle where the quantized weights header was mislabelled, causing the runtime to select a slower fallback execution path for some sequences (not directly causing corruption but made detection slower).

Timeline (UTC):
- 2025-11-06 20:58: deploy pipeline triggered for blueprint-v2.1 canary (deploy job #deploy-2193).
- 2025-11-06 21:14: first spike in chat-service 5xxs seen by alerting (rate from 0.02% to 0.7%).
- 2025-11-06 21:16 on-call (Maya) paged; paged SRE rotation.
- 2025-11-06 21:18 triage: error traces show tokenization exceptions and mismatched token IDs in responses (non-UTF8 bytes).
- 2025-11-06 21:22 Canary pool traffic routed to debugging instance for capture.
- 2025-11-06 21:30 Confirmed tokenizer mismatch: serving runtime loaded tokenizer metadata version 2.0 while model expected 2.1 (token-to-id map differences produced invalid token values).
- 2025-11-06 21:35 Rolled back canary to blueprint-v2.0; immediate error rates returned to baseline within ~90s.
- 2025-11-06 22:05 Post-rollback investigation started; opened SRE-842.
- 2025-11-07 09:00 Engineering reproduces locally with trimmed artifact and confirms packaging header issue for quantized weights (PR #2193).
- 2025-11-08 14:22 Hotfix: strict validation added to deployment pipeline to assert tokenizer version compatibility and token-vocab checksum; deployment pipeline updated.
- 2025-11-10 11:10 Drafting runbook changes and checklist (this doc).

Impact: 
- Customer-facing: negligible — canary was ~0.4% of total production requests; no broad user-facing outage.
- Internal: chat-service error rate increase tripped SLO alerts and generated on-call wakeups; increased customer support noise for ~20 requests.
- Operational: rollback required and additional validation work; temporary capacity to run extended canaries for validation.

Root cause analysis: 
1) Tokenizer version mismatch (primary):
   - The model artifact blueprint-v2.1 was packaged with tokenizer metadata indicating v2.1 mapping. The canary-serving env had a default tokenizer path set to tokenizers/latest which at the time of canary still pointed at vocab_v2.0 due to a prior config promotion that didn't update the symlink on canary hosts. The runtime loaded the environment tokenizer instead of the artifact-embedded tokenizer metadata because the serving config precedence order currently prefers environment override. That precedence is wrong for canaries where artifact-embedded metadata should take priority.

2) Config drift in canary environment (contributor):
   - A recent infra change (infra PR infra-1057) changed the tokenizers/latest symlink during a maintenance window; this propagated to canary nodes but not to the CI artifact metadata. No canary-specific ops step verified token vocab checksums post-deploy.

3) Model bundle header mislabel (contributor):
   - The quantized weights file in the model tarball had an incorrect header field (endianness/label bit flipped) that caused the runtime to detect a mismatch for some sequences and switch to a slower parse path. While this didn't directly corrupt tokens, it contributed to heterogeneous behavior and slowed the detection/diagnosis. PR #2193 fixes the packaging step.

Why automation didn't catch this: 
- Pre-deploy validations assert model checksums and presence of tokenizer files but do not validate tokenizer version compatibility with the serving environment.
- Canary smoke tests only sample end-to-end requests and check for response time and basic non-empty responses; they do not assert token id distributions or run a tokenizer compatibility assertion.

Immediate remediation (what we did during incident):
- Scoped rollback: removed blueprint-v2.1 from canary routing and returned canary traffic to blueprint-v2.0 at 21:35 UTC.
- Created SRE-842 and enlisted serving-runtime and infra owners.
- Captured full request/response traces and token dumps into a secure investigation bucket.
- Rolling audit across canary host tokenizers to confirm symlink state.

Runbook draft: Canary model rollout checklist (for inclusion in serving-runtime runbook) — DRAFT
- Pre-deploy validations (blocking):
  1) Artifact-embedded tokenizer metadata checksum matches artifact files (sha256).
  2) Deployment pipeline verifies artifact tokenizer version against environment available versions; if mismatch, fail pipeline unless artifact-embedded tokenizer is present and flagged to override.
  3) Tokenizer compatibility unit: run a deterministic tokenizer round-trip for 100 sample prompts from the workload. Fail if mismatch.
  4) Quantized weight header validation: verify packaging header signature and endianness flag.
- Canary smoke-run (post-deploy but pre-traffic):
  1) Start canary with 0% traffic and run 2k internal synthetic requests across typical input lengths (<=64, 64-512, >512 tokens).
  2) Validate token id distributions and ensure no non-UTF8 tokens.
  3) Raise the canary to 1% only if smoke-run passes.
- Monitoring and alerting updates:
  1) Add a tokenizer-consistency metric to runtime that emits a non-zero count when artifact tokenizer != loaded tokenizer.
  2) Add token-invalid-count alert (rate or absolute threshold).
  3) Add canary-specific SLI ignoring noisy downstream transient rejections (to avoid double-alerting).
- Rollback checklist (if token mismatch or invalid tokens detected):
  1) Pause canary traffic routing.
  2) Pin canary nodes to previous model.
  3) Capture traces and artifact bundles (forensics).
  4) Notify downstream teams and open customer-facing comms if >1% traffic affected.

On-call notes (less formal):
- Initial suspicion should be tokenizer -> check loaded tokenizer path on canary node (/opt/tokenizers/current and artifact metadata in /var/model-cache).
- If non-UTF8 token bytes present, do not attempt to re-encode in place — rotate out canary instance and capture artifacts.
- Quick rollback command: rdctl rollout set blueprint-v2.0 --target canary --force (requires SRE lead approval if >0.5% traffic).
- Contact points: Leo Park (runtime), Ivy Gonzales (infra), Aarav Singh (model packing).

Post-incident actions (owners + due dates):
- infra: ensure tokenizers/latest symlink promotion process is atomic and canary hosts have explicit canary symlink; due 2025-11-17 — owner Ivy Gonzales.
- runtime: change config precedence so artifact-embedded tokenizer metadata overrides environment unless explicitly disabled; due 2025-11-14 — owner Leo Park.
- ci/cd: add tokenizer-version check to deploy pipeline and fail on mismatch; due 2025-11-12 — owner Aarav Singh (PR #2193).
- monitoring: add tokenizer-consistency metric and token-invalid-count alerts; due 2025-11-21 — owner Nora Bennett.
- docs: update serving-runtime runbook with canary checklist and rollback commands; due 2025-11-14 — owner Maya Chen.

Follow-up verification plan:
- Run an extended canary for blueprint-v2.1 only after the above mitigations are in place: 0% -> smoke-run -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> full. Each step requires token-distribution sanity checks.
- Run a retrospective (SRE + runtime + infra + model pack) on 2025-11-12 to review root cause and finalize runbook changes.

Lessons learned and recommendations:
- Precedence rules that prefer environment overrides over artifact metadata are unsafe for model+tokenizer coupling; artifact metadata must be authoritative for tokenizer mapping.
- Canary environments must be immutable with respect to per-model dependencies (or at least have explicit version pinning).
- Small packaging header issues can dramatically complicate debugging; strengthen packaging contract and add header checksums.
- Add chaos tests in staging that intentionally swap tokenizer versions to verify detection and alerting.

Notes for future SRE rotations:
- Keep a short checklist copy in the on-call Slack pinned messages for quick commands.
- Consider adding a lightweight local "tokenizer sanity" endpoint in the runtime that returns tokenizer name, version, and checksum for a running model.

Appendix: quick diagnostic commands (canary host):
- cat /var/model-cache/blueprint-v2.1/tokenizer/metadata.json
- rdctl runtime status --host canary-03 --model blueprint-v2.1
- sha256sum /opt/tokenizers/current/vocab_v2.1.json /var/model-cache/blueprint-v2.1/tokenizer/vocab.json
- rdctl rollout set blueprint-v2.0 --target canary --force

End of draft.

Attachments: token-dumps and traces uploaded to secure bucket s3://redwood-forensics/2025-11-06-canary-tokenizer-dumps/ (access only to SRE+runtime+infra).
